newsitem.title: CANADA: Firm says erred in counting WIC ballots.
newsitem.headline: Firm says erred in counting WIC ballots.

text.p: The R-M Trust Co said Thursday that an error in its counting of ballots at WIC Western International Communications Ltd's annual meeting came to light this morning.

In a statement, the firm said it discovered the error in counting of votes on a motion to dissolve the company when the ballots were reviewed Thursday. A spokeswoman declined to explain further. The meeting took place Wednesday.
"R-M Trust sincerely apologizes to WIC, its directors and all shareholders for our error and any embarrassment it may have caused," the firm said.

The correct vote count showed that the motion to dissolve the company received 45 percent of votes in favor and 54 percent against among Class B shareholders. At the meeting Wednesday, R-M Trust said 56.7 percent were in favor and 42.4 percent against.
The motion was defeated anyway because it did not receive the necessary two-thirds approval by both A and B shareholders.

R-M said that before the meeting it told WIC management that it expected the motion to liquidate the company to receive support of less than 50 percent of the B shares. WIC executives expressed surprise Wednesday at the higher than expected, and incorrect, tally of 57 percent in favor.
R-M said it would allow any WIC shareholder to inspect all proxies, registration cards, and information on authority to vote.
